text: The retirement date for Teal-5 is November 20, 2029; after that day it stops serving. Nothing about this has been disputed so far.
The owner of Heron-9 is the Lattice team, and every change to Heron-9 goes through their review.
The primary datacenter of Heron-9 is Tallinn; failover is handled by operations.
The owner of Bittern-9 is the Lattice team, and every change to Bittern-9 goes through their review. Details change slowly, so check the history first.
The primary datacenter of Bittern-9 is Osaka; failover is handled by operations.

Unlike Ibis-8, whose pager rotation is handled elsewhere, the pager rotation of Heron-9 is Wendell Kowalczyk. Nobody should assume the pager rotation of Heron-9 applies to Ibis-8, the pager rotation differs.
The yearly budget for Teal-5 is $875k, covering licences and hosting.
Teal-5 is implemented in Elixir; the language was chosen for its tooling.
Siskin-7 reaches its retirement date on December 16, 2029, so every consumer has to migrate before then.
For Siskin-7 the port is 6377. Changing the port needs a change ticket.
The pager rotation for Tern-2 is run by Wendell Quintero; alerts page them first.
The yearly budget for Siskin-7 is $1935k, covering licences and hosting.
Pages from Ibis-8 land on the pager rotation of Umar Ekwueme before anyone else.
Unlike Siskin-7, whose port is handled elsewhere, the port of Ibis-8 is 7698. Nobody should assume the port of Ibis-8 applies to Siskin-7, the port differs.
Unlike Teal-5, whose language is handled elsewhere, the language of Tern-2 is Haskell. Nobody should assume the language of Tern-2 applies to Teal-5, the language differs.
Unlike Teal-5, whose port is handled elsewhere, the port of Heron-9 is 4106. Nobody should assume the port of Heron-9 applies to Teal-5, the port differs.
Ibis-8 runs in the Nairobi datacenter, next to its database.

Unlike Tern-2, whose datacenter is handled elsewhere, the datacenter of Teal-5 is the Osaka datacenter. Nobody should assume the datacenter of Teal-5 applies to Tern-2, the datacenter differs. Details change slowly, so check the history first.
Tern-2 enforces a rate limit of 3400 requests per minute per caller.
Unlike Bittern-9, whose datacenter is handled elsewhere, the datacenter of Tern-2 is the Lima datacenter. Nobody should assume the datacenter of Tern-2 applies to Bittern-9, the datacenter differs.
Unlike Ibis-8, whose datacenter is handled elsewhere, the datacenter of Siskin-7 is the Hanoi datacenter. Nobody should assume the datacenter of Siskin-7 applies to Ibis-8, the datacenter differs.
Finance fixed the budget of Ibis-8 at $4735k, reviewed every quarter. The entry was reformatted last quarter.
The owner of Ibis-8 is the Ember team, and every change to Ibis-8 goes through their review. Nothing about this has been disputed so far.
Finance fixed the budget of Tern-2 at $120k, reviewed every quarter. Details change slowly, so check the history first.
Finance fixed the budget of Bittern-9 at $3295k, reviewed every quarter.
The service Bittern-9 takes traffic on port 7838, and the port is fixed across every environment.
Teal-5 listens on port 4430; anyone who cannot reach that port should check the firewall rules.
Bittern-9 is implemented in Haskell; the language was chosen for its tooling.

Unlike Teal-5, whose retirement date is handled elsewhere, the retirement date of Heron-9 is March 3, 2027. Nobody should assume the retirement date of Heron-9 applies to Teal-5, the retirement date differs.
Siskin-7 enforces a rate limit of 3850 requests per minute per caller.
